steps.q: Demand is now growing much faster than before. Are firms' existing factories and machines enough to keep meeting it for long?
steps.right: No, idle machines soon run out
steps.hint: If output has to keep rising faster and faster, does the same machinery stay sufficient?

steps.q: With no spare capacity left and orders still rising, what must a car factory do to produce even more?
steps.right: Buy more machines and build more capacity
steps.wrong: Just ask workers to work slightly harder
steps.hint: If capacity is used up, can small effort from workers add much more output?

steps.q: A UK car maker suddenly gets far more orders from buyers overseas. Does it now have a reason to build a new production line?
steps.right: Yes, to meet the extra overseas orders
steps.wrong: No, overseas orders don't affect its output plans
steps.hint: Where are the extra sales coming from, and can existing capacity cope?
